summary: Best val_bpb 0.977161 (cell best), down from the 0.997359 baseline: DEPTH 8, dim 768 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, 6 heads x 128), sliding window 256 on the S layers, value embeddings on the first 3 and last 3 layers, batch 197K tokens (device batch 96, accum 1). What worked was width at fixed shallow depth: holding DEPTH=8 and walking dim 512 -> 640 -> 768 gave 0.987984 -> 0.983912 -> 0.981339, and my width-only decomposition of a1's depth-10/dim-640 win (0.983912 vs their 0.985426, at 20% lower FLOPs) is what showed depth was the wrong axis. What did not work: more, smaller heads (HEAD_DIM 64 = 1.003287, a clear regression); trading MLP width for depth at fixed matrix FLOPs (depth 12 / MLP 2x = 0.991259); and, in my final run, a4's 197K batch, which is worth -0.0045 on a narrow long-window model but is worth exactly nothing (0.00001) once width is 768 and the window is 256. Width is also capped -- dim 896 at depth 8 failed twice for peers. Next I would leave shape alone and attack the two things nobody got traction on: the LR/warmdown surface re-tuned specifically for the dim-768 shape (all the LRs are still the dim-768-scaled defaults tuned at a different shape), and GQA or a cheaper unembedding to buy back the step time that width 896 could not afford.
